title: Dolly Parton's estate has filed a lawsuit against her nephew. Here's what's happened so far
summary: Bryan Seaver, Dolly Parton’s nephew and longtime head of security, is embroiled in a nasty and very public legal battle with the company managing her estate.

image.caption: Bryan Seaver, Dolly Parton’s nephew and longtime head of security, is embroiled in a nasty and very public legal battle with the company managing her estate, which is worth an estimated $450 million US. (A.M. Stewart /AFP/Getty Images, dollyparton/Instagram)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Bryan Seaver, Dolly Parton’s nephew and longtime head of security, is embroiled in a nasty and very public legal battle with the company managing her estate.
Legal battle continues over estate worth estimated $450 million US
At its heart, the dispute appears to be about — what else? — money.
Forbes estimated that Parton, whose death from cancer was announced on Aug. 25, had a net worth of $450 million US.

While neither she nor her late husband Carl Dean had any children, Parton did have a large family — 11 siblings (six of whom are still alive), at least 12 nephews and nieces, according to People magazine, and even some great-nephews and -nieces.
She’s Alive, LLC is the name of the entity created to manage and protect Parton’s estate. It’s run by her longtime manager Danny Nozell.
The estate has also filed a lawsuit and restraining order against Seaver, the family member Parton had handpicked to announce her death.

Bryan Seaver was fired from his job providing security at Dolly Parton's properties, including Dollywood, last month, and ordered to immediately vacate the premises. (Melissa Sue Gerrits/Getty Images)
Want to know more? Here’s how the dispute has played out so far:
Aug. 25: Dolly Parton dies after a brief battle with cancer. Bryan Seaver announces her death to the public in a short video statement on her Instagram account.
Sept. 9: She’s Alive, LLC is created.
Sept. 21: TMZ reports Seaver has been fired from providing security services at Parton’s properties.

A copy of the termination letter obtained by the tabloid indicates Seaver and his staff were ordered to vacate the properties immediately. It says the decision was made "for the protection of the Trust and beneficiaries as a whole." It also states Seaver’s personal stake in the estate is not being terminated.
Sept. 22: She’s Alive files a lawsuit and temporary restraining order against Seaver.

TMZ publishes court documents filed by Parton’s former manager, Danny Nozell, alleging Seaver described himself as an international arms dealer, and raised his military experience to intimidate Nozell into giving him money.
Seaver denies he threatened Nozell, telling TMZ "a lot of these messages are two guys having rage talk and crying on the phone together while we were grieving."
Voicemail from Dolly Parton showed 'how much she cares': Singer
Sept. 23: A Tennessee judge rules Seaver and his company show a "present and continuing disruption and threat" to She's Alive.

Parton’s sister Freida says there is no feud within her family on Facebook. "No one among the Parton/Owens family is fighting over Dolly’s estate," she says in the post. "We all love Bryan, just as we all love each other."

Oct. 2: Seaver asks a Tennessee court to delay a hearing scheduled for Oct. 9, saying he has been unable to find a lawyer to represent him. TMZ reports every attorney he approached had ties to Pinnacle Bank — which is involved with the trust at the centre of the estate battle — thus creating a conflict of interest.

Oct. 5: She’s Alive asks the court to deny Seaver’s motion and submits documents describing how he attempted to evade the person hired to serve him legal documents. They allege Seaver went so far as to put a no-trespassing sign in his front yard and drape barbed wire across the handrails leading to his front door.
Seaver’s next hearing is scheduled for Oct. 20. It’s still not clear if he has found a lawyer to represent him.
